See conflict C1. ## Files likely to change - `scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py` - `tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_post_capture_evolution.py` - `.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml` - `tests/test_pr_checks_workflow.py` - `changelog.d/9930-fingerprint-base-deletion-supersede.md` (new) - `agents.d/9930-fingerprint-base-deletion-supersede.md` (new) ## Acceptance ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_post_capture_evolution.py::test_base_deletion_supersedes_missing_must_contain_in_merge_working_tree red-on-base ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_post_capture_evolution.py::test_base_deletion_supersede_in_compare_against_baseline_mode red-on-base ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_post_capture_evolution.py::test_base_deletion_resolver_deleted_path_still_fails ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_post_capture_evolution.py::test_base_deletion_flag_off_keeps_strict_violation ACCEPTANCE: test tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_post_capture_evolution.py::test_base_deletion_history_error_fails_closed ACCEPTANCE: post-merge none: the verifier runs inside later integration-sync conflict-resolver runs, not in a dedicated post-merge workflow ## Functions or modules to implement ### 1. `scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py` Follow the existing `_is_must_contain_post_capture_evolution_false_positive` pattern (lines ~532-662): same caching, fail-closed `subprocess` handling, `GIT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECS`, and `_AI_MERGE_RESOLVE_SUBJECT_PREFIX` attribution. New module-level items (`grep` found no `BASE_DELETION` / `base_deletion` identifiers in `scripts/`): - `_BASE_DELETION_SUPERSEDE_ENV = "INTEGRATION_FINGERPRINT_BASE_DELETION_SUPERSEDE_ENABLED"`. - `_BASE_DELETION_SUPERSEDE_CACHE: dict[tuple[str, str, str], str | None]`, keyed on (history_ref, normalized_path, captured_at). - `_BASE_DELETION_FLAG_WARNED: bool = False`, so the invalid-value warning is logged once per process. `_base_deletion_supersede_enabled() -> bool` - Reads the env var and strips it. Unset, empty, or `true` (any case) → True. `false` (any case) → False. - Any other value → False, plus one `::warning::verify_integration_fingerprints: invalid INTEGRATION_FINGERPRINT_BASE_DELETION_SUPERSEDE_ENABLED=; base-deletion supersede disabled.` printed to **stderr**. Stderr keeps the `--list-violated-files` stdout contract. `_resolve_base_deletion_history_ref(ref: str | None) -> tuple[str, str] | None` Returns (git_rev, label) or None. Order: 1. **Ref mode** (`_normalize_ref(ref)` not None, i.e. the wave-dispatch gate verifying the integration branch HEAD): use the verified ref itself. Once a resolver merge of the base lands, the base's history is reachable from it. 2. **Working-tree mode with a merge in progress**: `git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD^{commit}` succeeds → use that SHA, label `MERGE_HEAD`. The integration-sync resolver keeps `MERGE_HEAD` until its commit (`scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh` ~4659/4760), and that is the base side being merged in. 3. **Working-tree mode without a merge**: env `BASE_BRANCH` is set, matches a safe ref-name check (no `..`, no leading `-`, no whitespace), and `git rev-parse -q --verify refs/remotes/origin/^{commit}` succeeds → use it. `review_conflict_resolve.sh:1825` already uses `refs/remotes/origin/${BASE_BRANCH}`. This reads an existing variable; no new env var. 4. Otherwise → None, and the defense does not apply (fail closed). Any subprocess exception or nonzero exit → None. `_base_deletion_superseding_commit(ref, captured_at, path) -> tuple[str, str] | None` Returns (deleting_commit_sha, history_label) or None. Fails closed throughout: - Flag off → None. - `_captured_at_to_epoch(captured_at)` is None → None. - `_normalize_repo_path(path)` returns an error → None. - `_resolve_base_deletion_history_ref` returns None → None. - Cache lookup. - Absence at the history tip: `git ls-tree --name-only -- `. A nonzero exit or exception → None (history check errored). Non-empty output → None (the base still has the path, so the base did not delete it). - Newest deletion: `git log --no-renames --diff-filter=D --max-count=1 --format=%H%x00%ct%x00%s -- `. No `--first-parent`, so the base's own non-merge deletion commit is found through the resolver merge's second parent. `--no-renames` makes a move show as a deletion. Merge commits show no diff by default in `git log`, so a resolver merge never counts as the deleter. A nonzero exit, exception, empty output, or unparseable line → None. - Accept only when `commit_epoch > captured_epoch` and the subject does not start with `[ai-merge-resolve]`. Otherwise None. - Cache and return. `_evaluate_fp_state(...)` changes - Add keyword parameter `deletion_captured_at: Any = None`. Effective value: `deletion_captured_at if deletion_captured_at is not None else captured_at`. The new defense uses only this value; existing defenses keep reading `captured_at` unchanged (see D3). - In the `kind == "must_contain"` branch, at the `if content is None:` block (~line 1426), before returning the "file does not exist in post-resolve tree" violation, call `_base_deletion_superseding_commit(ref, effective, path)`.
